title: Field-valued point classes and the map from scheme points
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $F$ a presheaf of sets on the category of schemes over $S$, with test schemes and universes as in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. A field-valued point representative is a field $K$ [def-weil-field], a map $s:\operatorname{Spec}K\to S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and an element $x\in F(\operatorname{Spec}K,s)$. Two representatives are equivalent when their restrictions to a common field extension agree, compatibly with their maps to $S$. The set $|F|$ of point classes is their quotient by this relation. For a scheme $T$ over $S$ and a morphism $t:h_T\to F$, the map $|t|:|T|\to|F|$ sends a scheme point $x$ to the class represented by $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to T\to F$.
